title: VPC Onboarding, Upgrade and Air-Gapped Acceptance Criteria (network contracts & operational flows)
creator: Sofia Alvarez
background: Customers running Redwood Private in isolated VPCs and air-gapped datacenters have repeatedly requested a single, prescriptive contract that defines allowed network paths, upgrade probes, artifact verification, and a minimal online footprint during onboarding and upgrades. Current acceptance notes are fragmented across multiple PRDs; this ticket consolidates requirements into an operational acceptance checklist and test plan for engineering and solutions teams.
goals: Define a single network & upgrade acceptance contract for new VPC customers (non-privileged workflows)
Ensure upgrades can be performed with zero- or minimal-egress options and a validated offline fallback path
Provide automated pre-upgrade validation and post-upgrade health checks that can run inside customer networks
Document runbooks and guardrails for safe rollback when network constraints or artifact validation fails
non_goals: Designing custom per-customer egress proxies (we will document interfaces and constraints instead)
Rewriting the operator for full airgap-only installs (engineering follow-up may split this into a separate workstream)
Hardcoding cloud-provider-specific network rules (we will provide canonical examples for AWS/Azure/GCP only)
requirements: Network contract: list of allowed outbound endpoints (domain or IP) required for control plane, image validation, and telemetry when egress is allowed
Minimal-eject path: support an upgrade path where only a single TLS handshake to a pre-authorized mirror is required
Offline artifact verification: support signed image bundles and an operator command to validate signatures locally without contacting external services
Time sync: acceptance requires NTP/chrony availability or a validated local RTC; upgrades must detect time skew > 5s and fail-safe
DNS model: support split-horizon DNS and allow operator-side hostname overrides for package mirrors
KMS integration: documented KMS key rotation sequencing for users who manage keys behind a private VPC gateway
Canary within VPC: support a one-node canary workflow that runs upgrade steps and health checks before cluster-wide rollout
Operator safe-mode: operator must be able to enter a read-only safe-mode that rolls back artifact installation on failure
Audit & logs: all upgrade steps must produce signed audit events stored locally with optional upload when egress is permitted
Timeouts & retries: any external fetch attempts must use a configurable backoff and total timeout bounded by the customer SLA window
acceptance_criteria: Given a customer VPC with no outbound internet (air-gapped), the operator can install and validate a pre-signed bundle from a local mirror or mounted image within 60 minutes for a 3-node cluster

Given a VPC with restricted egress allowing a single FQDN and IP range, the operator completes upgrade with only those endpoints contacted and reports the contacted endpoints in the upgrade audit logs
A pre-upgrade validation command (redwoodctl validate-network) returns pass/warn/fail and enumerates missing TCP/UDP ports, DNS records, and NTP status
During a canary upgrade, health checks (model serving probe, KV cache validation, latency smoke tests) must pass on the canary node for 10 minutes before the rollout proceeds
If artifact signature validation fails, the operator aborts the upgrade, writes a signed local audit event, and triggers the rollback plan with no partial state applied
Time skew detection prevents token requests to KMS and fails the upgrade with a clearly actionable error and remediation guidance

All acceptance steps are automatable via the private deploy CI harness and have corresponding end-to-end tests in the repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-e2e/tree/main/tests/onboarding-upgrades
Documentation: Solutions Engineer can follow the runbook (link below) to onboard a customer and complete an upgrade within the documented SLA without additional engineering changes
test_plan: Create a synthetic VPC testbed with three modes: full-egress, single-endpoint egress, and pure-airgap. Run the full upgrade matrix against stable and canary bundles
Simulate KMS key rotation mid-upgrade and verify rollback triggers and recovery path
Validate operator safe-mode by inducing a signature mismatch and confirming local audit log generation
Exercise split-horizon DNS by serving different mirror IPs and verifying operator hostname overrides are respected
Run latency and KV-cache consistency checks pre/post-upgrade with the test harness and validate thresholds are within SLO
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Internal validation using private-e2e harness (QA) in all three network modes
Phase 1: Beta with 2 pilot customers that require minimal changes to their on-prem networking
Phase 2: Public docs and support playbook release, include template firewall rules and sample manifest for local mirror sync
Phase 3: GA and closed-loop monitoring enabled in Console with upgrade telemetry dashboards
dependencies: ENG-13722: audit-events local signing and storage (planned)
PM-57384: offline artifact staging kmsg rotation (referenced for KMS sequencing)
open_questions: Should the pre-authorized mirror FQDN require mTLS with a customer-provided client cert or is TLS + token sufficient? (Security preference needed)
What is the acceptable maximum duration for an air-gapped full-cluster install beyond the 60-minute baseline for larger clusters?
Do we standardize on a single signed-bundle format (recommended) or support multiple packaging formats for backward compatibility?
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision: Prefer signed bundles and local signature verification over live checks to external artifact registries to minimize egress (favored by security and solutions teams)
Trade-off: Supporting physical media fallback increases operational complexity; we will document the procedure but defer automation to a separate engineering ticket
Decision: Canary within VPC chosen over blue-green due to network topology constraints and operator simplicity
